quandoUsar: Showcase for a small set of visual cards (rooms, products, plans) where one faces forward at a time and its neighbors appear in perspective.
Picking one item from a few, when the rest of the screen reacts to the front card: `onValueChange` reports which card the cylinder stops on.
quandoEvitar: Use `carousel` for a regular row of slides, with a page indicator and optional autoplay.
Use `card-stack` when the user decides card by card, discarding or choosing, with an undo option.
Avoid it with dozens of cards: the cylinder radius grows with the count and all cards stay mounted; a grid or list works better.

teclado.acao: With focus on the stage, rotate to the previous or next card; quick presses accumulate.
Rotate to the first or last card by the shortest path.
Moves through the stage, the front card's controls, and the previous and next buttons; the other cards are outside the focus order.
On the previous and next buttons, rotate one card.

acessibilidade: The root is a group with `aria-roledescription="carousel"` named by `label`; each card is a `slide` group labeled “N of M”, and only the front one is exposed: the others get `aria-hidden` and `inert`.
An `aria-live="polite"` region announces “Card N of M” on each change, and the previous and next buttons have their own `aria-label`.
Pass `label` with the name of the set; the other read-out texts (“Previous card”, “Card 2 of 8”) are hardcoded in English in the code.
movimento: The front card follows the drag point by point; on release, a fling carries the rotation slightly further and a spring with a slight overshoot settles it on the nearest card.
Cards darken as they move away from the front and the ones behind fade out; on entrance, the cylinder arrives spinning a little more than one card and stops on the initial one.
With “reduced motion”, the rotation jumps straight to the target card, with no spring or entrance, and the counter changes with only a fade.
responsivo: A `ResizeObserver` measures the stage: the card uses `cardWidth` or 58% of the available width, whichever is smaller, and the height shrinks in the same proportion.
The stage uses `touch-action: pan-y`: on touch, dragging horizontally rotates the cylinder and vertical page scrolling stays free.
desempenho: All cards stay mounted (the back ones are only hidden by `backface-visibility`) and each one follows the rotation to compute its own opacity; prefer few cards and light images.
notasIA: Each child becomes a card: pass three or more (with two, they become front and back; with no children, nothing is rendered).
Control it with `value` and `onValueChange` (index of the front card) or leave it uncontrolled with `defaultValue`; `onValueChange` fires when the target is decided, before the spring finishes.
Give the parent a width (the root takes 100%) and leave the height to `cardHeight` plus 96 px; inside the card, mark with `data-no-drag` the areas that must not start the drag.

quandoUsar: A few parts of a whole (up to about six), when each slice's share matters more than the exact comparison between values.
Switching between datasets with the same keys (month by month, plan by plan): the arcs transform instead of redrawing.
When the user needs to hide categories in the legend to see how the rest of the ring redistributes.
quandoEvitar: Use `composition-chart` when the space is a horizontal strip: the same parts fit in a stacked bar with a legend.
Use `treemap` when there are many parts or hierarchy levels; here, whatever falls below `groupBelow` or beyond `maxSegments` is grouped into “Other”.
Use `gauge` for a single value against a known range; the donut splits a total into parts.

teclado.acao: Move focus between the legend rows, wrapping at the ends; the focused row highlights the arc and appears in the center.
Go to the first and last legend rows.
In the legend, hide or show the segment (`legendAction="toggle"`) or pin it as selected (`legendAction="select"`).
Clears the pinned selection.

acessibilidade: The SVG is decorative (`aria-hidden`): the screen reader gets a summary with the total and slices, a hidden table with segment, value, and share, and `aria-live` announcements when a segment is shown or hidden.

Each legend row is a button with `aria-pressed` and an `aria-label` with name, value, and percentage; with `legend={false}`, the ring becomes a focusable group where the arrow keys read each segment and `Enter` or `Space` pins it.
`label` is required and names the figure; the texts generated for screen readers (“hidden”, “Segment”, “Includes…”) are hardcoded in English.
movimento: The first time 35% of the chart enters the viewport, the arcs open from the top in a single sweep, with each arc's trailing edge a moment behind the previous one.

When `data` changes or a segment is hidden, each arc moves from where it is to the new angle on a spring with no overshoot; equal keys keep position and color, and the segment that leaves closes until it disappears.
The active segment slides outward and thickens while the others fade, and the center changes its readout by rolling like a drum; with “reduced motion”, all of this changes instantly.
responsivo: The figure is a container (`container-type: inline-size`): at 460 px or more the legend sits beside the ring; below that, it goes underneath.
The ring is `size` px in diameter (208 by default) and shrinks to fit narrower containers; long labels in the center are truncated with an ellipsis.
desempenho: During animations, shapes are written straight to the DOM, one paint per frame, and numbers straight to the text: no frame re-renders React.
notasIA: `label` is required, and each item in `data` needs a stable `key`, `label`, and `value`; zero or negative values are discarded.

Selection (`activeKey`, `onActiveChange`) and hidden segments (`hiddenKeys`, `onHiddenKeysChange`) can be controlled or uncontrolled; the cursor only previews, clicking an arc pins or releases the selection, and the last visible segment is never hidden.
Colors follow `--series-1` through `--series-4` and then neutral tones (pass `color` on the item to go beyond); a parent with a width is enough, since the height comes from the content.

quandoUsar: A list, table, or search with nothing to show, with a short explanation and the next step (create, import, clear filters).
First use of an area of the product, when no item exists yet.
When the result of an action swaps the message in place: changing `title`, `description`, or `icon` transforms the content without remounting the block.
quandoEvitar: Use `empty-states` when you want the illustrated version, where shapes transform from one scene to another.
Use `skeleton` while content is still loading; an empty state is for when the response arrived and there are no items.
Use `alert` for errors and warnings the user needs to recover from.
acessibilidade: The root is a `<section>`; pass `label` to make it a named region, useful when the page has more than one empty state.
The title is always an `<h3>`: check that this level fits the page's heading hierarchy.
The icon is `aria-hidden` and, during a swap, so is the outgoing copy, so the screen reader doesn't read the old text along with the new.
movimento: On first appearance only the icon box enters, with a fade and a slight scale-up.
When `title`, `description`, or the icon change, the new text rises out of a slight blur while the old one leaves, the icon cross-fades, and the block height follows a spring.
With “reduced motion”, swaps become a quick fade and the height changes instantly.
responsivo: It takes 100% of the parent's width, with vertical padding between `--space-8` and `--space-12` depending on screen width; the description is capped at 18rem and wraps in balanced lines.
Actions wrap and stay centered when they don't fit side by side.
notasIA: `title` and `description` are required strings (they serve as the animation key); `action` accepts any node, usually a `button`, and `icon` replaces the default folder.
To get the transition between states, keep the same `<EmptyState>` mounted and change the props; changing the `key` remounts the component and loses the effect.
The icon only cross-fades when the icon component changes (from `Folder` to `Check`, for example); use 24 px icons, like the default.

quandoUsar: File explorer for a project in an editor, code reviewer, or repository panel.
List of changed files, with each one's version-control mark (`status`: M, A, D, U) and the dot that flags folders with changes inside.
Trees the user navigates by keyboard only, jumping to a file by typing the start of its name.
quandoEvitar: Use `tree-view` for hierarchies that aren't files (categories, sections), with no per-extension icon or change marks.
Use `tree-table` when each row has columns, checkbox selection, or children loaded on demand.
Use `animated-sidebar` for app navigation with nested groups; this tree selects files, it doesn't switch pages.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next visible row, skipping disabled ones.
`→` opens the folder or, if already open, goes to its first item; `←` closes the folder or, on a file, goes back to the parent folder.
Go to the first and last visible rows.
Select the file or open and close the folder; `Enter` on a file also calls `onOpen`.
Opens all sibling folders of the focused row.
Typing the start of a name (letters, numbers, or a dot) moves focus to the matching row; repeating the same key cycles through the ones that start with it.

acessibilidade: Follows the tree pattern: `role="tree"` named by `label`, `treeitem` rows with `aria-level`, `aria-setsize`, and `aria-posinset`, `aria-expanded` on folders, and `aria-selected` on files.
Only one row is in the `Tab` order (the focused one, otherwise the selected one, otherwise the first); nodes with `disabled` remain visible, but the keyboard skips them and they can't be selected.
The status letter carries its full name for screen readers and a folder with changes says “contains changes”; these texts and “Empty folder” are hardcoded in English.
movimento: Opening a folder animates the group's height on a spring with no overshoot, and rows enter in sequence, sliding 8 px from the left, with the total delay capped at 0.2 s.
The arrow rotates 90°, the icon shrinks slightly when pressed, and the selected row gets a highlight bar that grows from the middle.
With “reduced motion”, folders open and close instantly and the arrow, icon, and bar transitions are turned off.
responsivo: Long names are truncated with an ellipsis; each level indents 1rem (`--tree-indent`) and each row is 1.875rem tall (`--tree-row`).
The tree doesn't scroll on its own: put it in a container with a height and scrolling (for example `scroll-area`) when there are many files.
desempenho: Closed folders don't render their children, but there is no virtualization: each visible row is an element; keep `nodes` referentially stable, since the visible list is recomputed when it changes.
notasIA: A folder is any node with `children` (use `[]` for an empty folder); the default `id` is the path from the root, like `src/app/page.tsx`, and that is what goes in `value` and `expandedIds`.
Selection (`value`, `onValueChange`) and open folders (`expandedIds`, `onExpandedChange`) support controlled or uncontrolled use; `onOpen` is separate and fires on `Enter` or double click on a file.
By default folders only open and close: pass `selectFolders` to make them selectable too; the icon comes from the name's extension or from `icon` on the node.

quandoUsar: Above a table or list, to show active filters as removable chips and clear them all at once.
When the user adds filters by choosing the field first and then the value, without leaving the bar (`addFilter`).
Collections with a few filter fields and one value per field: the added chip uses the field's `id`, so a new choice replaces the previous one.
quandoEvitar: Use `chip-group` when the options are few and can stay always visible as toggle chips.
Use `multi-select` when a single field needs several values; here each field holds only one.
Use `search-field` for free-text search; the menu here only offers predefined values.

teclado.acao: Open the “Add filter” menu with focus on the first field and, inside it, choose the focused item.
On the button, open the menu on the first or last item; inside the menu, move focus, wrapping at the ends.
Go to the first and last menu items; typing letters jumps to the item that starts with them.
`→` enters the values of the focused field; `←` goes back to the field list.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the button that opened it.
Moves through each chip's remove button and the bar's actions; leaving the open menu with `Tab` closes it.

acessibilidade: The bar is a `role="group"` named by `label`; each remove button has an `aria-label` with field and value, and a `role="status"` region announces filters added, changed, and removed.
When removing a chip by keyboard, focus moves to the neighboring chip or, if the list empties, to the “Add filter” button; when the menu closes, focus returns to that button.
The menu is a `role="dialog"` with `role="menu"` lists (`menuitemradio` on values) and a single `Tab` stop per list; the fixed texts (“Clear all”, “No filters applied”, “Remove…”) are in English.
movimento: Each chip opens and closes its own width space on a spring, so neighbors and actions slide along; a chip that moves to another line slides there, and the bar's height follows.

The “Add filter” button grows into the menu panel (width, height, and position on the same spring) and returns faster on close; the field and value steps slide in following the direction of navigation.
With “reduced motion”, chips, panel, and steps swap instantly or with a short fade.
responsivo: On screens up to 520 px the bar becomes a column, with chips on top and actions below, right-aligned; chips always wrap and long labels are truncated.
The menu panel opens upward when there's no room below, shifts to fit the window or the ancestor that clips content, and scrolls internally above `min(20rem, 55vh)`.
desempenho: Line wraps are animated by size observers on each chip and a `MutationObserver` on the list, and only in the 0.9 s following a filter change; resizing the window animates nothing.
notasIA: It is fully controlled: keep `filters` in state and update it in `onRemove`, `onClearAll`, and `addFilter.onAdd`; in `onAdd`, replace the chip with the same `id`, which is the field's `id`.
The chip received in `onAdd` carries in `value` the option's displayed text (its `label`), not its `value`; always pass `onClearAll`, because the “Clear all” button appears even without it.
The panel doesn't use a portal: avoid `overflow: hidden` on ancestors; `children` goes between the add button and “Clear all”, and `FilterMenu` is also exported for standalone use.

quandoUsar: A fixed sequence of stages (checkout, signup, onboarding) where the question is how many move from each stage to the next.
Comparing the same funnel across segments or periods by swapping `data`: stages with the same `key` transform to the new width.
Reports where the percentage drop between stages and the overall conversion must stay visible, without depending on the cursor.
quandoEvitar: Use `sankey-chart` when the flow splits or merges across several nodes, instead of following a single queue of stages.
Use `stepper` to show which step a person is on in a flow; the funnel shows how many reached each stage.
Use `composition-chart` or `donut-chart` when the values are parts of a whole, not stages where each contains the next.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, move to the previous or next stage and show its tooltip; `←` and `→` do the same.
Go to the first and last stage.
Removes the highlight from the current stage.
The chart is a single `Tab` stop: on receiving focus by keyboard, it highlights the first stage; on losing it, none.

acessibilidade: A focusable vertical `role="slider"` sits over the chart, and its `aria-valuetext` describes the current stage: name, value, share of the first stage, and drop from the previous one.
The drawing, labels, and tooltip are `aria-hidden`; the same numbers are in a hidden table with stage, value, share of the first stage, and drop.
`label` is required and names the figure; the fixed texts (“overall conversion”, “Reached”, “dropped off before this stage”) are in English.
movimento: When 30% of the chart enters the viewport, the bars grow from the center outward, one stage after another, from top to bottom, followed by the tapers and the drop pills; the numbers count up from zero.
After that, swapping `data` transforms all stages at once, and the tooltip slides from stage to stage on a spring while the others fade.
With “reduced motion”, the chart appears ready and swaps are instant.
responsivo: Width is measured with `ResizeObserver` and the drawing uses real pixels; the label column spans 84 px to 176 px (at most 34% of the width) and long names are truncated.
Height grows with the number of stages (44 px of `stageHeight` plus 28 px of `connectorHeight` by default); on touch, tapping a stage shows the tooltip and vertical scrolling stays free.
notasIA: `label` is required; pass `data` in stage order, with a stable `key`: each bar's width is relative to the largest value, and the percentages are relative to the first stage and the previous one.
Pass values that don't grow from one stage to the next: the component doesn't validate this, and the drop would come out negative.

Only the width comes from the parent; to control the highlighted stage use `activeKey` with `onActiveChange` (without updating the state, the cursor does nothing), and `hideHeader` removes the header with the overall conversion.

quandoUsar: A single value against a known range on a dashboard: server load, support score, quota usage.
When the value has named states (healthy, busy, critical): with `thresholds`, color and label change the instant the number crosses each limit.
quandoEvitar: Use `progress` for the progress of a task with a known end, such as a file upload.
Use `usage-meter` when it matters to see what fills a quota and how much remains before the limit.
Use `slider` when the user needs to adjust the value; the gauge is read-only.
acessibilidade: The ring is a `role="meter"` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax`, `aria-valuenow`, and an `aria-valuetext` with the percentage and the band name; the drawing and the animated number are `aria-hidden`.
Each `thresholds` band has a text `label`, so the state doesn't depend on color alone.
`label` is required; the figure's `aria-label` joins label, value, and maximum with a fixed English “of”.
movimento: The first fill waits until half of the gauge enters the viewport: the arc closes slowly, without overshooting the value, while the number counts up.

On each new value, the arc and number move there on a spring; the band's color and label change when the on-screen number crosses the limit, and the text enters from below if the value rose or from above if it fell.
With “reduced motion”, the arc and number jump to the value and the texts swap with a quick fade.
responsivo: The ring takes `min(100%, 176px)` of width and the stroke thickness scales with it; there is no size prop, so the parent's width decides.
notasIA: The center always shows the percentage within the range (`7.4` between 0 and 10 appears as 74%), not the raw value; use `detail` to state the value with its unit.
In `thresholds`, the band with the highest `from` that the value reaches applies: include one with `from` equal to `min` so there is always a state; without `thresholds`, the color comes from `tone`.
It accepts neither `className` nor a size: wrap it in a container with the width you want, remembering that the ring doesn't exceed 176 px.

quandoUsar: Before and after an edit: photo retouching, a screen redesign, the result of a filter or an upscale.
Two versions of the same scene with the same framing (maps, renders, screenshots), where the difference shows when sliding the divider.
quandoEvitar: Avoid it when the images have different proportions or framing: both are cropped to cover the same frame, and the point-by-point comparison is lost.
Use `image-viewer` to zoom and browse several images.
Use `file-diff` to compare versions of text or code.

teclado.acao: Move the divider 1% left or right; in vertical orientation, use `↑` and `↓`.
Move the divider in 10% steps.
Also move 10% at a time.
`Home` shows only the before image; `End`, only the after image.
Moves focus to the divider handle.

acessibilidade: The handle is a `role="slider"` named by `label`, with `aria-orientation` and a value from 0 to 100 that says how much of the after image is visible (the `aria-valuetext` “N% after” is hardcoded in English).
The captions over the images are `aria-hidden`: pass images with their own `alt` in `before` and `after`.
Clicking or dragging on the photo moves focus to the handle, so the arrow keys work right afterward.
movimento: The handle follows the drag point by point, gives like an elastic past the edges, and stays where it was released; a click on the photo moves the divider there on a spring.
During the drag the round handle becomes a capsule and its arrows move apart; changing `orientation` rotates the divider a quarter turn instead of switching the layout at once.
With “reduced motion”, the divider jumps to the position, with no spring or elastic, and the orientation change is immediate.
responsivo: The frame takes 100% of the parent's width and the height comes from `aspectRatio` (default `3 / 2`); images, `picture`, and videos passed in are fitted to cover it.

On touch, a finger on the photo waits for a drag along the divider's axis before taking over the gesture, so the page keeps scrolling; the handle responds immediately and has a touch area larger than the visible circle.
desempenho: During the drag the position runs on motion values, and `onPositionChange` fires at most once per whole percentage point.
notasIA: `before` and `after` are nodes: pass `` (or `picture`, video) with the same framing; the component already applies width, height, and `object-fit: cover`.
`position` is the percentage from the left (or top): control it with `onPositionChange` or leave it uncontrolled with `defaultPosition`; a double click on the handle resets to 50.
`labels={false}` hides the captions, `labels` with two texts replaces them (the default is “Before” and “After”), and `aspectRatio` accepts any CSS value, such as `"4 / 3"`.

quandoUsar: Photo gallery (product, travel, portfolio, attachments) where the user opens an image, zooms in, and moves to the neighboring ones.
When opening the image should preserve the sense of place: the thumbnail grows into the image and returns to the same spot on close.
Images with a short caption that call for zoom by mouse wheel, pinch, double click, or keyboard.
quandoEvitar: Use `carousel` to move through slides within the page itself, without opening a full-screen layer.
Use `image-compare` to compare two versions of the same image.
Use `infinite-masonry` for a long feed of varying heights that loads more on scroll; here the grid has fixed columns and mounts all thumbnails.

teclado.acao: On a thumbnail, open the viewer on that image.
Go to the previous or next image; with `loop`, wrap at the ends.
Go to the first and last image.
Zoom in and out in 1.6× steps, up to `maxZoom`; `=` also zooms in and `0` returns to the fitted size.
Closes the viewer: the image returns to the thumbnail and so does focus.
Cycle through the viewer's controls (zoom, close, arrows, thumbnail strip) without leaving it.

acessibilidade: The viewer is a Radix dialog: it traps focus, closes with `Esc`, and on close returns focus to the thumbnail of the last image viewed.
Each thumbnail is a button with `aria-label` “Open image N of M: alt”, and the `aria-live` counter announces the current image on each change.
Provide `alt` on all images (it names the buttons and is read in the counter) and `label` for the gallery; the control labels are hardcoded in English.
movimento: The pressed thumbnail grows on a spring to the size fitted to the screen and returns faster on close; if it is offscreen, the image only fades.
Between images, the new one enters from the side of the movement; the drag follows the finger, resists when there is nowhere to go, and switches images past the threshold or on a fling.
With “reduced motion”, opening, closing, and switching become a fade, and zoom by button or key jumps straight to the level.
responsivo: The grid always keeps `columns` columns (3 by default), with no breakpoints: adjust the prop according to the available width.
Below 640 px the side arrows disappear and navigation is by swipe and the thumbnail strip, which scrolls horizontally; the image's side margins drop from 84 px to 12 px.
desempenho: Grid thumbnails use `loading="lazy"`; pass `thumbnail` with a smaller file, which also serves as a preview while the full image loads.
Provide `width` and `height` so the viewer knows the aspect before loading; the thumbnail strip mounts all images at once, so very large galleries are heavy.
notasIA: The component renders the grid and the viewer: pass `images` with `src` and `alt`, and preferably `thumbnail`, `width`, `height`, and `caption`.
`value` is the index of the open image or `null` (closed): control it with `onValueChange`, which receives the index on open or switch and `null` on close, or use `defaultValue`.
The viewer opens in a full-screen portal (`position: fixed`, `z-index` 80 and 81); `className` applies only to the thumbnail grid.

quandoUsar: Inspecting API responses, webhook events, or log records in internal tools and debugging panels.
When the user needs to find a key or value in a large object: search highlights the matches and opens the branches that contain them.
When a field's path matters: the current row shows its own (`order.items[0].sku`) and offers actions to copy the value or the path.
quandoEvitar: Use `code-block` to show a short JSON snippet as static code.
Use `tree-view` to navigate a hierarchy of items with their own labels; here each row is always a key and a value.
Use `sortable-data-table` when the JSON is a list of records with the same fields, which compare better in columns.

teclado.acao: Move the current row; `Home` and `End` go to the first and last.
`→` opens the branch or, if already open, goes to the first child; `←` closes the branch or goes back to the parent.
Open or close the branch; on the “Show N more” row, load the next page.
Moves focus to the search field.
In the search field, go to the next and previous match; `Esc` clears the search and `↓` returns to the tree.
Trigger copying the focused row's value; with `Shift`, its path.

acessibilidade: Follows the WAI-ARIA tree pattern: `role="tree"` named by `label` and `treeitem` rows with level, position, `aria-expanded`, and an `aria-label` that summarizes key, type, and value; only the current row is in the `Tab` order.
The search match count is `aria-live`, and the result of each copy (success or failure) is announced in a `role="status"` region.
The row copy buttons are outside the `Tab` order (by keyboard, use the shortcut) and the one on the path bar is focusable; the interface texts are hardcoded in English.
movimento: When opening or closing a branch, loading a page, or expanding everything, each row unfolds its own height on a spring with no overshoot, with a fade.
The current row's highlight slides from one row to another, and the scrolling that keeps that row in view (or centers a search match) uses the same spring.
With “reduced motion”, rows, highlight, and scrolling change instantly; above 400 visible rows, row animation is turned off for everyone.
responsivo: The tree scrolls internally, limited by `maxHeight` (420 px by default); rows don't wrap, long values are truncated with an ellipsis, and strings over 40 characters show the full text in the `title`.
On screens up to 420 px the per-level indent drops from 16 px to 12 px, keys take at most 40% of the row, and the type disappears from the path bar.
desempenho: Long arrays and objects enter in pages of `pageSize` (50 by default) with a “Show N more” row; there is no virtualization, so each visible row is an element.
Search scans the entire JSON on every keystroke and stops at 2,000 matches; with very large payloads, typing can lag.
notasIA: Pass the already-parsed value (object or array) in `data`, not the JSON text: a string would appear as a single value.

Paths start from `rootName` (default `root`), like `root.users[0].name`: this is the format that `expanded`, `defaultExpanded`, `onSelect`, and `onCopy` use, and `defaultExpandDepth` opens the first levels.

It already comes with its own border, background, and scrolling (`maxHeight`), so it doesn't need another card around it; `searchable`, `copyable`, and `showPath` turn off search, copy, and the path bar.

quandoUsar: One or more measures over time, when the shape of the trend matters more than an isolated value.
Comparing the current period with the previous one or with a target, using a dashed series (`dashed`).
Dashboards with a range switch (7, 14, 30 days): with the same `key`s, the lines transform instead of redrawing.
quandoEvitar: Use `sparkline` for a compact trend next to a number, with no axes or legend.
Use `bar-chart` to compare a measure period by period, reading each bar against the average.
Use `brush-chart` for dense series where the user needs to zoom into a time window.

teclado.acao: With focus on the chart, move the crosshair to the previous or next point; `↓` and `↑` do the same.
`Page Up` moves forward and `Page Down` moves back about a sixth of the points.
Go to the first and last point.
Releases the crosshair and hides the tooltip.
On the legend buttons, hide or show the series.
Moves through the legend buttons and the chart; on receiving focus by keyboard, the crosshair starts at the most recent point.

acessibilidade: The chart area is a `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` reads the current point with the value of each visible series; SVG, axes, and tooltip are `aria-hidden`.
There is a hidden summary with the range and the last value of each series, and a hidden table with all points, whose first column uses `categoryLabel`.
The legend buttons use `aria-pressed`, and a hidden series gets a struck-through name, not just a missing color; `label` is required, and `loading` marks the figure with `aria-busy`.
movimento: The first time it enters the viewport with data, the lines draw from left to right in about 0.8 s.
Swapping `data` transforms each line from its current shape, even with a different number of points, while the scale and gridlines readjust; hiding a series flattens it to the baseline.
The crosshair slides between points and the tooltip follows it on its own spring, switching sides before leaving the chart; with “reduced motion”, all of this is immediate.
responsivo: The width follows the container and the height is fixed by the `height` prop (220 px by default); the value axis takes 48 px on the right.
The date axis shows at most one label every 76 px, counting from the most recent; on touch, pressing and dragging horizontally moves the crosshair.
desempenho: A single painter writes the paths straight to the SVG on each frame, without re-rendering React; the hidden screen-reader table has one row per point, which is heavy with thousands of points.
notasIA: `label`, `data`, and `series` are required; each point carries `values` indexed by the series `key`, and a missing value counts as zero, not as a gap.
Only points with `axisLabel` get an axis label; the first series uses the accent color with a filled area, and the rest stay in neutral tones until they receive `color`.
Use `onActiveChange` to feed a highlight number outside the chart and `loading` to keep the current lines faded while the next range loads.

quandoUsar: Trading screens that show how resting liquidity was distributed by price over time.
Finding order walls and seeing where they sit relative to the traded price, drawn as a line over the grid (`path`).
quandoEvitar: Use `order-book` to see the current buy and sell offers, with cumulative depth and spread.
Use `volume-profile` for volume traded per price level, in a histogram beside the price line.
Use `activity-heatmap` for per-day activity on a calendar; here the axes are always time and price.

teclado.acao: Move the readout one time column back or forward.
Go up or down one price level.
Go up or down four price levels.
Go to the first and last column, at the same price.
Releases the cell and returns to the readout of the most recent column.

acessibilidade: The chart is a focusable `role="application"`, described as “heatmap”, with a hidden usage hint; each keyboard movement announces time, price, and size in a `role="status"` region.
The SVG is `aria-hidden` and there is no alternative table: values are read cell by cell by keyboard, and the summary above the grid shows time, price, and size of the cell being read.
`label` is required; the interface labels (“Latest”, “Resting size”, “Traded price”) are hardcoded in English, and `locale` only changes the number format.
movimento: When 30% of the chart enters the viewport, the columns appear from left to right, rising 8 px, and then the traded price line draws over them.
With new data, cells change color in the same sweep; the bands and the crosshair ring slide on a spring to the cell being read, and the legend marker follows the color step.
With “reduced motion”, the grid and the line appear ready and the crosshair jumps from cell to cell.
responsivo: The chart measures its own width and draws in real pixels; the height is the `height` prop (268 px, time axis included), and the price strip on the right adjusts to the longest label.
Axis labels thin out as cells shrink, and in containers up to 400 px the summary and legend become more compact.
desempenho: Each cell is a `<rect>` in the SVG (columns × levels; the demo uses 48 × 24 = 1,152): the grid is memoized while reading with the cursor, but is rebuilt on every data or width change.
notasIA: `values` is indexed as `values[tempo][preço]`, aligned with `times` and `prices`; prices can come in any order, but must be evenly spaced.
Fix `max` when the data updates, otherwise the color scale is recomputed from the largest value of each set; `path` is optional and carries the traded price of each column.
Pass memoized arrays: the model is recomputed whenever `times`, `prices`, or `values` change identity; `onCellChange` receives the cell being read or `null` when the reading returns to rest.

quandoUsar: Row of customer logos, short testimonials, or a news ticker that serves as ambiance, not essential content.
Vertical activity feed that scrolls slowly in a fixed-height space (`direction="up"`).
quandoEvitar: Use `logo-marquee` when you want the ready-made row of brands, already with a pause control.
Use `carousel` when the user needs to stop on each item and control the progression.
Use `announcement-bar` for important notices at the top of the page; essential information must not depend on moving text.
acessibilidade: The repetitions carry `aria-hidden` and `inert`, so each item is read and receives focus only once; with `label`, the root becomes a named `role="group"`.

With `pauseOnHover` (default), the cursor over the strip or focus inside it makes it slow down until it stops; for motion that lasts more than a few seconds, also provide a pause button tied to `paused`.
movimento: The content runs at `speed` px per second in an animation-frame loop and repeats as many times as needed (up to 24 copies) to join seamlessly.
Pausing and resuming go through a spring that takes the pace from 1 to 0 and back, so the strip brakes and accelerates instead of freezing; offscreen, it rests.
With “reduced motion”, nothing moves on its own: the copies aren't rendered and the strip becomes a regular scroll area, keyboard-focusable.
responsivo: The strip takes the parent's width and recalculates the number of copies when it or the content changes size.
In the `up` and `down` directions the root uses `height: 100%`: the parent must have a defined height.
desempenho: Each instance runs a frame loop (`useAnimationFrame`) that only moves a `transform`; the children are rendered in every copy, so avoid heavy items or ones with their own state and effects.
notasIA: Pass the items as direct children: the marquee lays them out in a row (or column) and applies `gap` between them and between repetitions.
`speed` is in px per second (48 by default), `direction` accepts `left`, `right`, `up`, and `down`, and `fade` controls the edge mask (`true`, a CSS length like `"28%"`, or `false`).
To pause with a button, keep a state and pass it to `paused`: the component doesn't include that button.

quandoUsar: Summary of indicators at the top of a dashboard: a number with a label, comparison context, and change.
Numbers that change with a filter or period: the digits roll to the new value and the texts enter from the side the number moved toward.
quandoEvitar: Use `animated-counter` when the animated number alone is enough, with no card, label, or context.
Use `stats-band` for highlight numbers on a marketing page.
Use `gauge` or `usage-meter` when the value only makes sense against a range or a limit.
acessibilidade: The animated number is `aria-hidden` and the final formatted value goes in a hidden text, so the screen reader reads the correct number in one go.
The card is an `<article>` with no heading of its own (the label is plain text): give the section that groups the cards a heading if the page needs that structure.
The change is colored by sign, but the `+` or `-` itself in the text already conveys the direction, without relying on color alone.
movimento: The digits roll from zero the first time the number enters the viewport; after that, each column rolls in the direction the value changed.
When `label`, `context`, or `change` change, the new text enters from below if its number rose or from above if it fell, and the change pill adjusts its width on a spring.
With “reduced motion”, the digits jump to the value and the texts swap with a quick fade.
responsivo: The card takes the parent's width; on screens up to 380 px the inner padding shrinks and the change pill may move to the line below.
notasIA: `value` is numeric and appears as an integer with a thousands separator in the `en-US` format: the card doesn't forward `decimals`, `prefix`, or `locale` to the counter, so put the currency in `label` and the unit in `suffix`.
`label`, `value`, and `context` are required; `change` is free text: if it starts with `+` it turns green and with `-` red, with no way to invert for metrics where a drop is good.
It needs the `animated-counter` item installed (the card imports it from `../animated-counter/animated-counter`); for a row of indicators, put the cards in a grid, since each one fills its own cell.

quandoUsar: Trading screen that shows the current buy and sell offers, with cumulative depth, spread, and the mid price between the best offers.
Letting the user pick a limit order's price by clicking a level (`onSelectLevel`).
Demos and sample screens for trading products, with the simulated feed `useOrderBookFeed`.
quandoEvitar: Use `liquidity-heatmap` to see how liquidity evolved over time, not just the current snapshot.
Use `candlestick-chart` for price history in candles.
Use `sortable-data-table` for generic record tables with sorting; the book has fixed columns and order.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the level above or below, on the same side.
Switch to the buy side or the sell side, on the same row.
Go to the best price and to the last level of the current side.
Select the row's price; on the already selected row, clear the selection.
The whole book is a single `Tab` stop; the arrow keys do the rest.

acessibilidade: The root is a `role="group"` named by `label`, with two labeled lists (buys and sells, best price first); each row is a button with `aria-pressed` and an `aria-label` with side, price, size, and total.

Focus on a row does the same as the cursor: it highlights the levels up to it and shows in the footer how much it costs to trade up to there; feed changes are not announced, since there is no live region.
`label` is required; headers and phrases (“Bid”, “Ask”, “Spread”, “at an average of”) are hardcoded in English, and `locale` only changes the number format.
movimento: When a level's size changes, the row flashes for 0.6 s: in the side's color if it grew, in a neutral tone if it shrank.
When the price moves, rows slide to their new position on a spring, new ones enter fading in, and the depth bars stretch from the middle of the book.
With “reduced motion”, there is no flash or slide, and `useOrderBookFeed` stops emitting updates.
responsivo: The root is a container: at 520 px or more each side gets the cumulative total column; at up to 360 px the row padding shrinks and, at up to 300 px, so does the font.
The two sides always stay side by side; below 520 px the price column uses its own text width, so the size column is the one that shrinks.
desempenho: Rows are memoized and only `depth` levels per side are rendered; the simulated feed uses an interval (850 ms by default) that stops when the tab is hidden.
In a real high-frequency feed, batch the updates before swapping `bids` and `asks`: each swap recomputes the totals and triggers flashes and slides.
notasIA: Pass `bids` and `asks` as `{ price, size }` in any order: the component sorts, drops zero sizes, cuts at `depth`, and computes totals, spread, and the mid price.
`selectedPrice` controls the selection (`null` for none; `undefined` lets the book manage it), and `onSelectLevel` receives `{ side, price, size }` or `null` when the row is clicked again.
`useOrderBookFeed` is a seeded simulation for demos, not a market connection: with real data, pass your own arrays and keep prices rounded consistently, since they are each row's key.

quandoUsar: Tables and lists with a known number of pages, such as orders or search results.
When the user moves page by page or jumps between nearby pages: the window shows five numbers around the current one.
quandoEvitar: Use `infinite-masonry` for feeds that load more items as scrolling reaches the end.
Use `stepper` for the steps of a flow; pagination is for pages of a single collection.
Avoid it when the total number of pages is unknown (cursor-based APIs): the component requires `pageCount` and has no previous-and-next-only mode.

teclado.acao: Move through the previous button, the page numbers, and the next button.
Activate the focused button and call `onPageChange`.

acessibilidade: It is a `<nav>` named by `label` (default “Pagination”): give each pagination a different name when there is more than one on the page.
The current page gets `aria-current="page"`, each number has an `aria-label` “Page N”, and the arrows are `disabled` on the first and last page; these labels are hardcoded in English.
The items are buttons, not links: changing the URL or data is up to your `onPageChange`.
movimento: A single marker slides on a spring to the current page number.
When the five-number window shifts, the numbers move together like a conveyor belt, each by the same number of places, while the ones entering and leaving fade.
With “reduced motion”, the marker jumps and the numbers swap without sliding.
responsivo: There are at most seven 2.25rem buttons (two arrows and five numbers), about 276 px in total; if width runs short, the navigation wraps.
notasIA: It is controlled: keep `page` (starts at 1) in state and update it in `onPageChange`; there is no uncontrolled mode or `className`.
Compute `pageCount` with `Math.ceil(total / porPagina)`: the component rounds fractions down, and the last partial page would be unreachable.
Import with braces, from `@/components/ryan-ui/pagination/pagination` (there is no default export); there are no ellipses or shortcut to the first and last page, so show the total nearby.

quandoUsar: Showcase of a few image highlights (destinations, guides, projects, categories) where hovering shows the preview and pressing the open card leads to the detail.
Page sections where one item is always in the spotlight and the others appear as slices with the title.
quandoEvitar: Use `carousel` when there are many items or all need the same prominence; here, each additional card narrows the closed slices.
Use `image-viewer` to open and zoom photos.
Use `tabs` when each option reveals its own content (text, forms) instead of a short preview over an image.

teclado.acao: Move focus to the previous or next card, which opens on receiving focus; `↑` and `↓` do the same.
Go to the first and last card.
On the open card, call `onSelect`.
Each card is a `Tab` stop, and focus opens the card.

acessibilidade: The rail is a `role="group"` named by `label`; each card is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and the title in hidden text, and the preview texts enter the button's name when it opens.
Focus opens the card, so keyboard users see the same preview as the cursor; on touch, the first tap on a closed card only opens it, and the second selects it.
The image's `alt` is empty by default: fill in `alt` on the item only when the image says something the title doesn't.
movimento: Only `flex-grow` animates, on a spring with no overshoot: the open card grows to `ratio` times the width of a closed one, and the rest become slices.
The open card's image brightens, the vertical label disappears, and the preview lines rise 10 px in sequence.
With “reduced motion”, the width swaps instantly and the preview only fades.
responsivo: The root is a container: at up to 520 px the rail becomes a column, 1.5 times taller than `height`, and the open card grows vertically, with the closed cards' labels horizontal.
A closed card's width is the rail's width, minus the gaps, divided by `ratio` + number of items − 1; with many items, the slices become too narrow for the label.
desempenho: Animating `flex-grow` redoes the row's layout on every frame, so the image and preview are born at the open size and the card only reveals them; all images load immediately, without `loading="lazy"`.
notasIA: Each item needs `id`, `title`, and `image`; `eyebrow`, `description` (clamped to two lines), and `meta` are optional.

There is always one open card (the first, by default): `value` with `onValueChange` controls which, and `onSelect` fires when pressing the already open card; do the navigation in it, since the card is a button, not a link.
`trigger="press"` makes the mouse open cards only on click, not on hover (focus and touch still open them); `height` is in px, and the width comes from the parent.
